question: When does delayed harvest season start in North Carolina?
answer: North Carolina delayed harvest season begins October 1 and runs through the first Saturday of June. During this period catch-and-release only is required on all designated delayed harvest streams — including the Tuckasegee River through downtown Bryson City and the Upper Nantahala River. Only single-hook artificial lures are permitted. No natural bait may be possessed. NCWRC stocks delayed harvest sections in October, November, March, April, and May.

question: What is the best fly fishing on the Tuckasegee River in fall?
answer: The Tuckasegee River delayed harvest section through downtown Bryson City opens October 1 with fresh stockings of rainbow and brown trout — approximately 27,048 trout covering 2.2 miles of stream from Darnell Farms bridge to Mountain Ford bridge in town. Float trips on the Tuckasegee produce some of the highest fish counts of the entire year during fall delayed harvest. The river offers excellent fly fishing access by both wade and drift boat throughout the season.

question: What is the October Caddis and why is it important in fall fly fishing?
answer: The October Caddis is a large orange-bodied caddisfly that hatches in fall on the wild streams of Great Smoky Mountains National Park — triggering some of the most aggressive dry fly takes of the entire year from the largest brown trout in the system. Half a dozen of Mac Brown's personal best brown trout have fallen to large October Caddis patterns on the park streams. Large parachute patterns, elk hair caddis, and stimulators in sizes 8-12 produce best during peak October Caddis activity.

question: Is streamer fishing good on the Nantahala River in fall?
answer: Yes — fall is the prime streamer season on the Nantahala River as dropping water temperatures trigger aggressive predatory feeding behavior from the largest brown trout in the system. Some of the largest record brown trout on the Nantahala have fallen to streamers during fall conditions. Mac Brown has documented days on the lower Nantahala producing six brown trout over six pounds to the boat on a single guided float trip during fall streamer season.
